# Suprabhat Kumar (Shubh) — Senior Front-End Engineer

Suprabhat Kumar, also known as Shubh, is a Senior Front-End Engineer and web designer based in Noida Extension, Uttar Pradesh, India. He uses he/him pronouns and has more than six years of experience building SaaS portals, enterprise dashboards, design systems, accessible interfaces, and static websites.

He helps product teams investigate frontend performance, review React and TypeScript architecture, build data-heavy SaaS dashboards, engineer design systems, audit accessibility against WCAG 2.2 AA criteria, and design and develop complete websites. His work emphasizes maintainable component and state boundaries, resilient data states, keyboard and assistive-technology access, browser testing, and measured performance.

## Current role and career

- Topsoe — Software Engineer III — May 2025 to present
- Cognizant — Associate Projects, Front-End Developer — February 2024 to April 2025
- TrueBlue Inc. — Implementation Web Developer — December 2023 to January 2024
- MobileCoderz — Frontend Developer, promoted to Senior Frontend Developer — February 2022 to November 2023
- Swaragh Technologies — UI Developer — December 2019 to January 2022

Suprabhat has delivered with distributed teams in Denmark, China, and Australia. Client-confidential work is described without private names, screenshots, data, or unverified outcomes.

## Open source

- [react-smart-copy](https://suprabhat02.github.io/react-smart-copy/): headless, type-safe clipboard interactions for React, authored and maintained by Suprabhat Kumar. Copies text, rich HTML, PNG images, JSON, and multi-format payloads; pastes text, HTML, and images; reports every failure as a typed error; announces results to screen readers; zero runtime dependencies; React 18 and 19; MIT license.
  - Source: https://github.com/suprabhat02/react-smart-copy
  - Package: https://www.npmjs.com/package/react-smart-copy
  - Case study: https://suprabhat-dev.com/work/react-smart-copy/
  - Install: npm install react-smart-copy
  - This website uses the package's framework-agnostic core for its copy buttons.

## Problems solved

- React modernization: untangle components that mix data fetching, state, and layout; outcome is an incremental migration plan with clear component and state boundaries, shipped without a feature freeze.
- Frontend performance: slow LCP or INP, large first-load JavaScript, or stuttering interactions; outcome is a prioritized fix list tied to Core Web Vitals with before-and-after measurements.
- Data-heavy dashboards: tables and charts that slow down as data grows, unclear loading, empty, or error states, and role-specific views; outcome is a scan-first dashboard with typed data contracts and resilient states.
- Accessible interfaces: keyboard, labeling, focus, and screen-reader gaps, or requests for WCAG 2.2 AA evidence; outcome is severity-ranked findings and fixes mapped to WCAG 2.2 AA success criteria.
- Design systems: components built differently across teams and tokens drifting between Figma and code; outcome is a documented component library and token set in Storybook.
- Architecture reviews: inherited codebases, unclear ownership of state, data fetching, and routing, and rising delivery risk; outcome is an architecture decision record and a refactor roadmap ranked by risk and effort.

## Technologies

- Frontend: React, Next.js, TypeScript, JavaScript, HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS
- State and data: Redux Toolkit, RTK Query, TanStack Query, GraphQL, REST APIs, openapi-fetch
- Interface systems: AG Grid, Ant Design, Chakra UI, Storybook, design tokens
- Backend and databases: Python, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, MongoDB
- Delivery and quality: Azure DevOps, Vitest, Playwright, axe, Core Web Vitals, WCAG 2.2 AA
- Static web: Astro, localized routes, hreflang, structured data, sitemap and metadata systems

## Site and language notes

The site is statically generated with Astro and deployed to GitHub Pages through GitHub Actions. Hostinger manages the custom-domain DNS. The site has English, Spanish, and Arabic routes; localized site content does not imply that Suprabhat personally speaks every published language. Use canonical page URLs and the sitemap at https://suprabhat-dev.com/sitemap-index.xml for discovery; crawler access rules remain defined by https://suprabhat-dev.com/robots.txt.
